reasoning: B wins on the criteria that matter most for this task. Its confirmation is a real modal with outcome-named buttons, the safe option focused first, and both tap-outside and B cancelling. It reads both Roblox accessibility settings live and skips the fade when ReducedMotionEnabled is on, and B closes the dialog before the menu. A is solid and motion-free, but it never reads ReducedMotionEnabled, labels the safe button a generic 'Cancel', and closes the whole menu on B. Both attempts pass all three static checks; the failed clearMyBlocks check, and A's failed GameAudio check, come from passing the functions by reference, not from bugs.

criteria.note: VolumeSlider has −/+ step buttons (10% steps) that controllers can select, plus a track you can drag or tap. App passes GameAudio.setMusicVolume and setEffectsVolume in by reference.

The inline confirmation says the blocks 'can't be brought back' and the confirm button reads 'Delete them', but the safe button is plain 'Cancel'. Cancel only gets focus if selection was already active. B closes the whole menu rather than just the confirmation, though it never confirms.
The backdrop follows PreferredTransparency live and the panel is opaque. The menu has no animation at all, so it is motion-safe, but it never reads ReducedMotionEnabled.

Opening with a controller selects the Music minus button, the Panel is a SelectionGroup with Stop behaviors, and buttons fire on Activated. B always closes the whole menu instead of closing the confirmation first.
TouchTarget is 48 px. The open button sits at the top right with CoreUISafeInsets and IgnoreGuiInset=false, clear of the thumbstick, jump button, and top bar.

The percent label, fill, and knob update immediately and a status line reports 'Your blocks have been deleted.' There is no animation. Buttons change color on hover or selection only, with no pressed state.
Clean checks, ResetOnSpawn=false, block placing is turned off while open and restored on close, and the UI mounts before BlockPlacer.start. Y is always sunk at default priority.
volumeSlider has Lower/Raise step buttons that disable at 0 and 100% plus a draggable bar. App calls GameAudio.setMusicVolume and setEffectsVolume, then reads the getters back.

Modal confirmDialog titled 'Delete all your blocks?' says the blocks 'will be gone for good'. Buttons read 'Keep blocks' and 'Delete blocks', Cancel takes focus first, and both the outside backdrop and B call closeConfirm.
Screen.luau keeps both settings as live sources. The backdrop scales with preferredTransparency, and its 0.25 s spring fade is skipped when isReducedMotion is on.
Opening focuses the Music minus button. The panel is set non-Interactable while the dialog is open and both are SelectionGroups. backHandler closes the dialog first, then the menu.
TouchTarget is 56 px with a UIScale whose minimum is 1, and the Settings button sits at the top right with CoreUISafeInsets.
Fill and percent update immediately, buttons show a pressed color through GuiState and a yellow focus stroke, the description switches to 'Done. Your blocks were deleted.', and the fade is short.
Clean checks and a modal menu that also turns off touch controls. Small risks: Y returns Pass, Screen makes global connections, and BlockPlacer is re-enabled unconditionally on close.

strengths: Simple, readable components with clear comments
Opaque panel and no motion at all
Step buttons plus a draggable track for volume
weaknesses: Inline confirmation with a generic 'Cancel' label
B closes the whole menu instead of the confirmation first
Focus is not kept inside the confirmation area

strengths: Proper modal confirmation with outcome-named buttons and the safe option focused first
B steps back correctly: dialog first, then menu
Pressed and focus states on buttons, plus UIScale for different screens
weaknesses: More complex, with a global Screen module
fitScale can shrink controls below 44 px on very small screens
Y toggle passes the input on to other bindings instead of sinking it
